headline.caveat: Contract dollars undisclosed. Multi-year HBM3E/HBM4 supply to NVIDIA; Micron's HBM is sold out through 2026 with pricing largely locked under LTAs.

realized_to_date.caveat: Ongoing deliveries since 2024 (H200/Blackwell HBM3E); customer-level revenue not disclosed.

nature_md: Micron supplies HBM3E (since the H200/Blackwell generation) and HBM4 to NVIDIA under multi-year agreements with volumes and pricing undisclosed. Micron has said its HBM output is sold out through calendar 2026, and the AI memory cycle drove its FQ3-26 revenue to $41.5B (vs $9.3B a year earlier) at ~86% guided gross margin — figures that themselves signal how far contracted AI memory pricing has moved. NVIDIA allocation among the three HBM vendors is actively managed and competitive each generation.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: NVIDIA books HBM as input cost (COGS) on delivery; multi-year volume commitments appear within aggregate supply obligations. Prepayment specifics, if any, are not itemized.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Micron recognizes revenue on delivery under LTAs; sold-out-through-2026 means near-total revenue visibility, and HBM capex (Boise, Singapore) is effectively underwritten by committed AI demand.

observations.notes: vs $9.3B a year earlier; FQ4 guide ~$50B at ~86% GM. Not NVIDIA-specific, but NVIDIA is the anchor HBM customer.
